question.explanation:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

  • If $|8-2x| = 8-2x,$ we obtain: \begin{align} |8-2x| &= 5 \\[5pt] 8-2x &= 5 \\[5pt] -2x &= -3 \\[5pt] \dfrac{-2x}{-2} &= \dfrac{-3}{-2}\\[5pt] x &= \dfrac{3}{2} \end{align}

  • If $|8-2x| = -(8-2x),$ we obtain: \begin{align} |8-2x| &= 5 \\[5pt] -(8-2x) &= 5 \\[5pt] -8 + 2x &= 5 \\[5pt] 2x &= 13 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2x}{2} &= \dfrac{13}{2}\\[5pt] x &= \dfrac{13}{2} \end{align}

Therefore, the solutions are $x = \dfrac{3}{2}$ and $x = \dfrac{13}{2}.$

example.title: Solving Absolute Value Equations With Negative Variable Coefficients

question.explanation:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

  • If $\left|3 - \dfrac{2}{3}y\right| = 3 - \dfrac{2}{3}y,$ we obtain: \begin{align*} \left|3 - \dfrac{2}{3}y\right| & = 5 \\[5pt] 3 - \dfrac{2}{3}y & = 5\\[5pt] -\dfrac{2}{3}y & = 2 \end{align*} Multiplying both sides of the equation by $-\dfrac{3}{2}$ gives \begin{align*} \require{cancel} -\dfrac{2}{3}y & = 2 \\[5pt] \left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right) \cdot \left(-\dfrac{2}{3}y\right) & = \left(-\dfrac{3}{2}\right) \cdot (2) \\[5pt] \left(\cancel{-\dfrac{3}{2}}\right) \cdot \left(\cancel{-\dfrac{2}{3}}y\right) & = -\dfrac{6}{2}\\[5pt] y & = -3. \end{align*}

  • If $\left|3 - \dfrac{2}{3}y\right| = -\left(3 - \dfrac{2}{3}y\right),$ we obtain: \begin{align*} \left|3 - \dfrac{2}{3}y\right| & = 5 \\[5pt] -\left(3 - \dfrac{2}{3}y\right) & = 5 \\[5pt] -3 + \dfrac{2}{3}y &= 5 \\[5pt] \dfrac{2}{3}y &= 8 \end{align*} Multiplying both sides of the equation by $\dfrac{3}{2}$ gives \begin{align*} \require{cancel} \dfrac{2}{3}y & = 8 \\[5pt] \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) \cdot \left(\dfrac{2}{3}y \right) & = \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) \cdot (8) \\[5pt] \left(\cancel{\dfrac{3}{2}}\right) \cdot \left(\cancel{\dfrac{2}{3}}y \right) & = \dfrac{24}{2} \\[5pt] y & = 12. \end{align*}

Therefore, the solutions are $y = -3$ and $y = 12.$

example.title: Solving Two-Step Absolute Value Equations Containing Fractions

question.text: Written in ascending order, the solutions to $|5y-1| = 6$ are $y =$
question.explanation:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

  • If $|5y-1| = 5y-1,$ we obtain: \begin{align} |5y-1| & = 6\\[5pt] 5y-1 & = 6\\[5pt] 5y & = 7\\[5pt] \dfrac{5y}{5} & = \dfrac{7}{5}\\[5pt] y & = \dfrac{7}{5} \end{align}

  • If $|5y-1| = -(5y-1),$ we obtain: \begin{align} |5y-1| & = 6\\[5pt] -(5y-1) & = 6\\[5pt] -5y+1 & = 6\\[5pt] -5y & = 5\\[5pt] \dfrac{-5y}{-5} & = \dfrac{5}{-5}\\[5pt] y & = -1 \end{align}

Therefore, in ascending order, the solutions are $y = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-1}$ and $y = \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{7}{5}}.$
